heading: INT. COUNTY PAROLE OFFICE - OFFICER OKAFOR'S OFFICE - LATER

units.text: INT. COUNTY PAROLE OFFICE - OFFICER OKAFOR'S OFFICE - LATER
Ruth Okafor, 50s, reading glasses pushed up into gray braids, sits behind a desk piled with files, a cactus, a photograph of a boy in a graduation gown turned slightly away from the visitor's chair.
She is calm, almost bored.
She has done this four thousand times.
The man sits.
He puts the folder on the desk.
Mr. Voss. How's the job?
units.name: RUTH

units.text: Fine.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: The apartment?
units.name: RUTH

units.text: Fine.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: You've been fine for six weeks. I'm starting to think you're a fine person.
units.name: RUTH

units.text: He doesn't smile.
She turns a page.
Says here you missed your Thursday check-in.
units.name: RUTH

units.text: I called.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: You left a message with Deb. Deb doesn't write things down. Deb is a lovely woman and a terrible secretary.
units.name: RUTH

units.text: I was at work. They put me on a double.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: Did you bring a pay stub?
units.name: RUTH

units.text: He slides the folder across.
She opens it, flips, and stops.
Her eyebrows lift very slightly.
This isn't a pay stub.
units.name: RUTH

units.text: It's a photograph.
A school photo, a boy of about eight, missing a front tooth.
She looks at it a long time.
When she looks up, her voice is lower.
Where did you get this?
units.name: RUTH

units.text: Mailbox. Yesterday.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: It's not allowed. You know it's not allowed. The order says no contact.
units.name: RUTH

units.text: I didn't contact anybody. It came in the mail. I didn't do a thing.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: He leans forward.
For the first time his voice shakes, not much, just enough.
Somebody wants me to violate. That's all this is. Somebody wants me back inside.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: Who?
units.name: RUTH

units.text: He doesn't answer.
His hands, on his knees, have begun to tremble, and he presses them flat.
Mr. Voss, I need a name.
units.name: RUTH

units.text: Calvin.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: Excuse me?
units.name: RUTH

units.text: Calvin. My name's Calvin. Everybody calls me Voss like I'm a case number. I'd like, once, for somebody in this building to say it.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: She sets the photograph down, gently, and for a moment the whole office seems to hold its breath.
Deb's keyboard has stopped.
Somewhere a printer jams.
Calvin.
units.name: RUTH

units.text: He closes his eyes.
I'm going to make a call. You're going to sit right here. You are not in trouble.
units.name: RUTH

units.text: That's what they said last time.
units.name: CALVIN

units.text: She stands, takes the photograph, and walks to the door, and in the doorway she hesitates, and does not look back, and this is the last time the two of them will sit in the same room as strangers.
